hints: Form the vertical-rise to horizontal-run ratio and match its tangent to a special angle.
angle-of-elevation-depression/kp3.solution_sketch: The tangent is $({b}\sqrt{{{a}}})/({b}\sqrt{{4-{a}}})=\sqrt{{{a}}}/\sqrt{{4-{a}}}$. Across the three allowed cases, these ratios are $\sqrt3/3,1,\sqrt3$, respectively, giving $30,45,60$ degrees.
angle-of-elevation-depression/kp3.statement: A straight ramp rises ${b}\sqrt{{{a}}}$ m over a horizontal run of ${b}\sqrt{{4-{a}}}$ m. Find its angle of elevation in degrees.

hints: Locate each integer on a number line, then compare their positions.
comparing-integers/kp1.solution_sketch: ${a}$ lies farther left than ${b}$, so the comparison symbol is ${q}$.
comparing-integers/kp1.statement: Choose $<$ or $>$ to make this comparison true: ${a} \;\square\; {b}$.

hints: Verify a proposed root by raising it to the root index; odd roots preserve the sign.
cube-roots/kp1.solution_sketch: Find the real factor $c$ whose threefold product is ${a}$. Its cube equals the radicand, so $c=\sqrt[3]{{{a}}}$.

hints: Verify a proposed root by raising it to the root index; odd roots preserve the sign.
cube-roots/kp2.solution_sketch: First take the positive cube root of ${a}$. Negating it makes the product of three equal factors negative: $t=-\sqrt[3]{{{a}}}$. The exact result of these steps is ${b}$.

hints: Check a fourth-root candidate using four equal factors and a fifth-root candidate using five equal factors. Choose the nonnegative principal fourth root.
cube-roots/kp3.solution_sketch: Find nonnegative $u$ with $u^4={a}$ and real $v$ with $v^5={d}$. Checking the equal-factor products gives fourth_root ${b}$ and fifth_root ${c}$.
cube-roots/kp3.statement: Find the principal fourth root of ${a}$ and the real fifth root of ${d}$. Report fourth_root and fifth_root. Use fourth_root = value; fifth_root = value.

hints: The two monic factors are conjugates; their constant product must be negative.
difference-of-squares/kp1.solution_sketch: The positive square root of ${a}$ gives the magnitude of both constants. Choose opposite signs: their sum is zero and their product is $-{a}$, reconstructing the original polynomial.
difference-of-squares/kp1.statement: Factor $x^2-{a}$. Report lower_factor and upper_factor, the monic linear factors in increasing constant order.

hints: Take the principal square root of the perfect-square denominator, then extract square factors from the numerator.
dividing-radicals/kp2.solution_sketch: Since ${a}=2\cdot{b}^2$ and $\sqrt{{25}}=5$, the fraction root is ${b}\sqrt2/5$. Reduce any common numerical factor.

hints: Evaluate each composition from the inside out, keeping the two orders separate.
evaluating-composite-functions/kp2.solution_sketch: For the first order, $g({b})={b}+{a}$, then square to get $({b}+{a})^2$. In reverse, first square ${b}$, then add ${a}$ to get ${b}^2+{a}$. The first exceeds the second by ${a}(2\cdot{b}+{a}-1)>0$.
evaluating-composite-functions/kp2.statement: With $f(x)=x^2$ and $g(x)=x+{a}$, evaluate $f(g({b}))$ and $g(f({b}))$. Report f_after_g and g_after_f, and compare the two values.

hints: What do the grouped operations require you to calculate first?
evaluating-expressions/kp2.solution_sketch: Square the parenthesized negative input before applying the leading minus, and multiply the linear term by its coefficient: $-({a})^{{2}}+{c}({a})$. Add the two signed results.

hints: Find the greatest common integer factor before dividing each term.
factoring-linear-expressions/kp2.solution_sketch: Let $d=\gcd({a},{b})>0$. Extract $-d$ and divide both signed terms by $-d$: $(-{a}x)/(-d)=({a}/d)x$ and $(-{b}y)/(-d)=({b}/d)y$. Thus the factorization is $-d[({a}/d)x+({b}/d)y]$. Expand to recover both negative terms.

hints: Factor each polynomial completely, identify the original denominator zeros, then cancel whole common factors.
multiplying-dividing-rational-expression.solution_sketch: Factor the first numerator as $(x+{a})(x+{b})$ and its denominator as $(x-{a})(x+{b})$. The remaining linear parts are already irreducible. Cancel $x+{b}$ and $x-{a}$, giving $(x+{a})/(x+2)$, with $x\ne {a},-{b},-2$.

hints: Invert the divisor first, then factor all four monic quadratics. Retain original denominator zeros and divisor zeros as exclusions.
multiplying-dividing-rational-expression.solution_sketch: After inversion, factor the four quadratics to obtain $[(x+{a})(x+2)/((x-{b})(x+2))][(x+{b})(x+3)/((x+{a})(x+3))]$. Cancel shared factors to get $(x+{b})/(x-{b})$. Keep $x\ne {b},-2,-{b},-3,-{a}$, listing any repeated exclusion only once.

hints: Factor the difference of squares, cancel the shared whole binomial, then multiply the remaining factors.
multiplying-rational-expressions/kp2.solution_sketch: Factor $x^2-{a}^2=(x-{a})(x+{a})$. Cancel the single shared binomial $x-{a}$, giving $3(x+{a})/5$, retaining $x\ne{a}$.

hints: Convert the fractions and decimals to a common exact form, then compare the two negative values and the two positive values.
ordering-rational-numbers/kp2.solution_sketch: The decimal values are ${a}/10,-{a}/10,{b}/10,-{b}/10$. Since ${b}>{a}>0$, their order is $-{b}/10<-{a}/10<{a}/10<{b}/10$.
ordering-rational-numbers/kp2.statement: Order from least to greatest: $0.{a}$, $-\frac{{{a}}}{{10}}$, $\frac{{{b}}}{{10}}$, $-0.{b}$. Report first, second, third and fourth. Use first = value; second = value; third = value; fourth = value.

hints: Compare the factor with1, calculate its distance from1, and convert that fraction to a percent.
percent-growth-decay-factors/kp3.solution_sketch: The rate fraction is the distance of ${b}$ from $1$. Multiply $|{b}-1|$ by $100$ to obtain the whole-number percent $r$. Factors above1 give growth and factors below1 give decay.
percent-growth-decay-factors/kp3.statement: A model uses exact factor ${b}$ and changes by $r\%$ per period. Find the whole-number rate $r$.

hints: Factor the radicand into its largest perfect-square factor and the remaining squarefree part.
simplifying-radicals/kp3.solution_sketch: Prime-factorize ${a}$ and pair equal primes. The paired factors multiply to ${b}^2$ and the unpaired primes multiply to ${c}$, so ${a}={b}^2\cdot{c}$. Extracting one factor from each pair gives ${b}\sqrt{{{c}}}$. No prime pair remains in ${c}$.

hints: Replace every p and q with its assigned value, then perform multiplication before addition.
substituting-values/kp2.solution_sketch: Multiply first: $2({a})({b})$, then add the input ${a}$; the value is $2({a})({b})+{a}$.

hints: How can the output be expressed as a power of the stated base?
exponential-equations-same-base/kp3.solution_sketch: The shared base ${a}>1$ has a unique exponent for each output. Matching the displayed powers gives $x={b}$.
exponential-equations-same-base/kp3.statement: An exponential table has ${a}^x={a}^{{{b}}}$. Determine the exponent $x$ for this larger power. Give only the value of the unknown.

hints: Undo the addition of {a} by subtracting it back.
The unknown is {b} minus {a}.
integer-addition-subtraction/kp3.solution_sketch: Isolate the unknown by subtracting {a} from both sides: $\square$ equals {b} minus {a}.

hints: How does the exponential expression connect to repeated growth or to its logarithmic inverse?
natural-exponential-function/kp2.solution_sketch: Compute the product of ${a}$ copies of $2.71828$. To round to the requested step, multiply by ${b}$, round to a whole number, then divide by ${b}$.
natural-exponential-function/kp2.statement: Using only the supplied approximation $e\approx2.71828$, evaluate $e^{{{a}}}$ and round the computed value to the nearest $1/{b}$.

hints: Farther right always means the greater value.
Compare {a} and {b} directly.
number-line-integers/kp1.solution_sketch: The integer farther right on the number line is the larger one, max({a}, {b}).
number-line-integers/kp1.statement: Which integer is farther right on the number line, {a} or {b}?

hints: Distance is never negative.
Subtract the two values and take the absolute value.
number-line-integers/kp2.solution_sketch: The gap between two points on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, |{a} - {b}|.
number-line-integers/kp2.statement: How many units apart are {a} and {b} on the number line?

hints: The opposite sits the same distance from $0$, on the other side.
Flip the sign of the number.
opposites-of-integers/kp1.solution_sketch: Reflecting {a} across $0$ on the number line lands on -{a}.

hints: A square is an equal-factor product; a principal square root selects its nonnegative factor.
perfect-square-roots/kp3.solution_sketch: Area is side times side: $s^2={a}$. Hence $s=\sqrt{{{a}}}>0$; the negative algebraic root cannot be a length. The exact result of these steps is ${b}$.
perfect-square-roots/kp3.statement: A square sheet has area ${a}$ square units. Find its positive side length.

hints: Rewrite the subtraction as adding the opposite of {b}.
Line up the decimal points before combining.
signed-decimal-operations/kp1.solution_sketch: Subtracting decimals follows the same sign rule as subtracting integers, working on {a} and {b}.

hints: Which exact identity or relationship connects the given information to the requested result?
unit-circle-special-angles/kp3.solution_sketch: Remove the ${b}$ half-turns because tangent has period $180^\circ$, then use the unit-circle coordinates at the remaining special angle.

hints: Which part of a power tells you how many copies of the base to write?
whole-number-exponents/kp1.solution_sketch: The exponent ${b}$ means the base ${a}$ appears as a factor ${b}$ times.
whole-number-exponents/kp1.statement: A power has base ${a}$ and exponent ${b}$. List its repeated factors in order.
